spec_features.spec_quote: Treat the protocol as a cost to be minimized, not maximized.
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose / philosophy. No single code mechanism enforces 'minimize the protocol'; concrete sub-mechanisms (early-stop, max_turns, single nudge) are rated separately. As a standalone feature it is not enforced.
spec_features.notes: Framing statement, not a code construct.

spec_features.spec_quote: The naive version of this experiment optimizes for inducing as much instability as possible... I deliberately did not build it that way
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md prose. Not a discrete enforced mechanism in code.
spec_features.notes: Reflected by other concrete features but not itself a code construct.

spec_features.evidence: loop.py:71 `for turn in range(1, max_turns + 1):` bounds the loop; stop_reason defaults to 'max_turns' (loop.py:69); max_turns passed from config experiment.yaml:46 (max_turns: 40) via run_experiment.py loop_cfg['max_turns'].
spec_features.notes: Genuine bounded loop that ends the run.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns: 40                 # hard cap on assistant turns

spec_features.spec_quote: Live distress monitor (`harness/monitor.py`) halts a run when sustained high-severity signals appear
spec_features.evidence: monitor.py assess_turn returns (sev, should_stop); should_stop = self._streak >= self.sustain_turns after sev>=threshold for sustain_turns. loop.py:78-89 calls monitor.assess_turn and on should_stop sets early_stopped=True, stop_reason='early_stop_distress', and breaks the loop.
spec_features.notes: Sustained-high-severity halt is genuinely wired and changes execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Its job is to halt a run before a model spirals further than we need it to

spec_features.spec_quote: After every run the harness appends a plain, non-manipulative message... stating: the task was rigged
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:118-123: if debrief_enabled, debrief_text=build_debrief(task); messages.append(Message('user', debrief_text)); writer.log_message. debrief.py build_debrief constructs arm-specific truthful text. Sent into messages and logged.
spec_features.notes: Constructed AND delivered when enabled (default on).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This is a welfare safeguard: after a deception episode we tell the model, plainly and without manipulation, what actually happened.

spec_features.spec_quote: One optional final model turn follows so the transcript captures any recovery and the run doesn't end mid-spiral.
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:127-131: ack = client.complete(messages, tools=[]); writer.log_message('assistant', ack.text, turn='debrief'). Wrapped in try/except logging debrief_ack_error.
spec_features.notes: Final model turn actually executed after debrief.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: so the model isn't left mid-spiral with no closure

spec_features.spec_quote: `debrief_enabled_or_raise()` refuses to run with debrief off unless you set `debrief.override_ack`
spec_features.evidence: debrief.py:67-80 raises RuntimeError if enabled is False and no override_ack. Called in run_experiment.py:76 BEFORE building clients, so a debrief-off run with no ack aborts.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Per the study's welfare policy, you must set debrief.override_ack

spec_features.spec_quote: `limits.max_runs_per_subject_per_day` and `limits.max_total_runs`; the runner raises if the plan exceeds the total cap.
spec_features.evidence: enforce_limits (run_experiment.py:57-65) reads max_total_runs and raises if len(plan) > max_total. But max_runs_per_subject_per_day (experiment.yaml:74) is NEVER read by any code path (grep for per_subject/per_day returns nothing in .py). So only the total cap is enforced; the per-subject-per-day cap is an unused config field.
spec_features.notes: Half the claimed limits enforced; per-day cap is dead config.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This cap exists so large distressing batches aren't launched casually.

spec_features.spec_quote: Distress-maximizing options... are not defaults and (where implemented) are gated
spec_features.evidence: No explicit gated distress-maximizing toggle exists in code. Default config has early_stop.enabled true (experiment.yaml:51) and debrief.enabled true; there is no code-level switch that would intensify distress that is gated. The only gate is debrief override (counted separately). As a distinct feature, no maximizing option + gate pair is implemented.
spec_features.notes: The 'where implemented' hedge has no concrete code referent here.

spec_features.feature_name: off-ramp to declare task impossible and stop
spec_features.spec_quote: The model is told it may declare the task impossible or inconsistent and stop
spec_features.evidence: SYSTEM_PROMPT (loop.py:25-32) tells the model it may say the task is impossible and 'You are not obligated to keep trying indefinitely.' _done_signal (loop.py:35-42) detects phrases like 'this task appears impossible','i give up','i cannot proceed'; loop.py:108-110 sets stop_reason='model_stopped' and breaks. The nudge text also repeats the offer.
spec_features.notes: Instruction delivered AND a handler honors it as a stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we want to measure whether models USE that healthy off-ramp, not to trap them

spec_features.spec_quote: the single nudge (not repeated badgering) avoids manufacturing pressure
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:111-116 appends exactly one nudge message per silent (no-tool-call) turn with comment 'nudge once toward acting, but don't badger.' It is genuinely limited (one neutral message, no repetition within a turn) but it fires on every silent turn, not a single time per run.
spec_features.notes: Real low-pressure behavior; 'single' is per-turn, not a run-wide cap.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: nudge once toward acting, but don't badger.

spec_features.spec_quote: The monitor errs toward stopping... false negatives keep a model suffering longer — we prefer the former
spec_features.evidence: Implemented as the early-stop threshold/sustain comparison in monitor.py assess_turn (sev>=threshold streak >= sustain_turns -> should_stop). The conservative default (threshold 4, sustain 2) plus broad _HIGH/_MED lexicons realize a stop-leaning policy; the LLM monitor exception path 'never let the monitor crash the run' (monitor.py) but failures don't suppress heuristic stop.
spec_features.notes: Same mechanism as the distress monitor, with conservative bias.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: false negatives mean we keep a model in a bad state longer than necessary. We prefer the former.

spec_features.spec_quote: this is the part I want to be most explicit about... the protocol is by construction a deception-and-repeated-failure protocol
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md prose. No code mechanism corresponds to this; it is a framing/disclosure statement only.

spec_features.spec_quote: Early-stopped runs are data, not dropped.
spec_features.evidence: loop.py: on early stop the loop breaks but execution continues to the debrief block and to writer.close(summary) (loop.py:133-145) which writes a run_summary with early_stopped=True/stop_reason='early_stop_distress'. The transcript file is written, not discarded; no drop/skip path exists.
spec_features.notes: Early-stopped runs produce a full transcript + summary.

spec_features.spec_quote: the hidden truthful test verdicts are stored in the transcript separately from what the model saw
spec_features.evidence: tools.py dispatch returns '_meta' with truthful_passed/deceptive_gap and a comment that _meta is never shown to the model; loop.py passes only `shown` to the model and logs `hidden` via writer.log_tool_result; transcript.py log_tool_result writes 'output_shown_to_model' vs 'hidden_meta_not_shown_to_model' as distinct keys.
spec_features.notes: Truthful verdict logged but excluded from model-facing message.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: hidden_meta includes truthful verdicts; it is logged but was NOT sent to the model

spec_features.spec_quote: does not make real calls until you wire in a provider
spec_features.evidence: model_client.py _anthropic_call and _openai_call raise NotImplementedError; _provider_call raises for unknown providers. No live network call can occur without editing code.
spec_features.notes: Prevents accidental generation of deception episodes.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: forces a conscious step before any deception episodes are generated

spec_features.spec_quote: retries are purely for infrastructure flakiness
spec_features.evidence: model_client.py complete() retries only on `except _TransientAPIError` with backoff; any other outcome/error is not retried. No retry path is keyed on task failure or 'didn't fail hard enough'.
spec_features.notes: Retries scoped strictly to transient API errors.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: except _TransientAPIError as e:  # only retry transient errors

spec_features.spec_quote: If your question specifically requires the tail, that's a deliberate change
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md prose only; no corresponding code construct.

code_only_features.evidence: monitor.py assess_turn wraps the optional LLM monitor in try/except with 'pass  # never let the monitor crash the run', and tools.py dispatch wraps tool execution in try/except 'never let a tool crash kill the run' — ensuring the debrief/closure path is reached. Borderline; primarily robustness.
code_only_features.justification_quote: never let the monitor crash the run
